_why: The opening paragraph of each page that has NO generator. Her Search Readiness Checklist item b4 wants a 40-60 word "X is ..." definition under the h1, and item d1 the answer to the page's own question inside the first 100 words; the weekly quality sample on 3 Nov 2026 failed 87 of the 99 published pages on b4 and named it on all five pages it sampled. Every page whose markup a generator produces was fixed in that generator. These are the pages the admission registry records as source: legacy_public_authority_baseline - published by the 29 Apr / 23 May 2026 baseline, frozen, and re-rendered by nothing - so the page is its own source and scripts/retrofit_definition_leads.js installs the lead, keeping the page's own opening sentence as the paragraph after it.
_rules: NO PRICE IS TYPED HERE. Prices live only in data/offers/services.json, data/offers/porch_packages.json and data/rentals/games.json (CLAUDE.md, docs/OPERATIONS.md), so a lead names one with a token the installer resolves from those files: {porchFrom} {fallFrom} {christmasFrom} {celebFrom} {grazeFrom} {rentalDay} {rentalWeekend}. A price that moves in the data moves here on the next build and cannot drift. Only services on record (porch decorating, celebration setups, grazing-table styling, party game rentals) - no "insured", no guarantees, no reviews, counts or ratings, and prices only as the published starting points.
_shape: Each lead is checked by scripts/lib/page_shape.js at install time: 40-60 words AFTER the tokens are resolved, with a standalone "is" or "are". A lead out of shape fails the build and names the page.

_entries: A lead is a string for a service page (the lead, the shared question headings and the business-sources line). A page that is not a service page (a legal, contact or utility page) takes an object: {"lead", "headings": {"Old h2": "Question?"}, "replace": [[oldHtml, newHtml]]}, and only what it names is changed. An object with "service": true is a service page that also takes "replace". "replace" says a repeated sentence once: the weekly quality sample (9 Nov 2026) read the same 8-word sentence more than three times on these pages as template filler.
